numbering: IEEE first appearance in the explanatory report
scope: External academic and professional sources. The supplied model is the main benchmark; the adapted single-view control isolates added corner processing.

entries.title: You Only Look Once: Unified, Real-Time Object Detection
entries.venue: IEEE Conference on Computer Vision and Pattern Recognition (CVPR)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Redmon, S. Divvala, R. Girshick, and A. Farhadi, “You only look once: Unified, real-time object detection,” in Proc. IEEE Conf. Comput. Vis. Pattern Recognit. (CVPR), 2016, pp. 779–788, doi: 10.1109/CVPR.2016.91.
entries.supported_claim: The original YOLO formulates object detection as a single network that predicts bounding boxes and class probabilities from a complete image.
entries.limitation: This historical detector paper does not document the current pose implementation, its two-point output, or the accuracy of the cassette models.

supports: DOI in indexed primary IEEE record

entries.title: ObjectLab: Automated Diagnosis of Mislabeled Images in Object Detection Data
entries.venue: ICML Workshop on Data-centric Machine Learning Research
entries.ieee_entry: U. Tkachenko, A. Thyagarajan, and J. Mueller, “ObjectLab: Automated diagnosis of mislabeled images in object detection data,” in ICML Workshop on Data-centric Machine Learning Research, 2023. [Online]. Available: https://arxiv.org/abs/2309.00832
entries.supported_claim: ObjectLab uses model predictions to prioritize images that may contain missing, misplaced, or incorrectly classified bounding-box annotations for human review.
entries.limitation: A model-generated suspicion is not proof that an annotation is wrong; independent image inspection is still required, and the paper does not validate the project's corner labels.

entries.title: Noise-Aware Evaluation of Object Detectors
entries.venue: IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV)
entries.ieee_entry: J. Murrugarra-Llerena and C. R. Jung, “Noise-aware evaluation of object detectors,” in Proc. IEEE/CVF Winter Conf. Appl. Comput. Vis. (WACV), 2025, pp. 9322–9331, doi: 10.1109/WACV61041.2025.00903.
entries.supported_claim: Bounding-box annotation uncertainty can alter detector evaluation, particularly for small objects and restrictive overlap thresholds, motivating sensitivity analysis of disputed references.
entries.limitation: This does not justify moving reference annotations toward a preferred model's predictions or treating model agreement as ground truth.

entries.title: TIDE: A General Toolbox for Identifying Object Detection Errors
entries.ieee_entry: D. Bolya, S. Foley, J. Hays, and J. Hoffman, “TIDE: A general toolbox for identifying object detection errors,” in Computer Vision – ECCV 2020, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 12348. Springer, 2020, pp. 558–573, doi: 10.1007/978-3-030-58580-8_33.
entries.supported_claim: TIDE separates sources of object-detection and instance-segmentation error and measures their effects on average precision, encouraging diagnosis beyond a single aggregate score.
entries.limitation: The project's fixed-threshold missed, unmatched, and duplicate counts are not a full reproduction of TIDE's error-oracle analysis, and corner accuracy requires additional metrics.

entries.title: Simple Baselines for Human Pose Estimation and Tracking
entries.ieee_entry: B. Xiao, H. Wu, and Y. Wei, “Simple baselines for human pose estimation and tracking,” in Computer Vision – ECCV 2018, Lecture Notes in Computer Science, vol. 11210. Springer, 2018, pp. 472–487, doi: 10.1007/978-3-030-01231-1_29.
entries.supported_claim: A ResNet feature extractor and three learned upsampling layers predict Gaussian-supervised landmark heatmaps; the paper also uses original/reflected heatmap averaging and a quarter-cell decoding adjustment.
entries.limitation: The cassette models adapt the architecture to two points. Coordinate averaging differs from the paper’s heatmap averaging; published human-pose results do not establish cassette performance.

entries.supported_claim: PoseFix refines image-plus-initial-pose input and trains on synthetic pose errors informed by observed human-pose error distributions.
entries.limitation: The cassette hint model uses Gaussian-target MSE and peak decoding, and does not reproduce PoseFix’s synthetic-error distribution, one-hot/integral objective or full inference procedure.

entries.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
entries.ieee_entry: C. Guo, G. Pleiss, Y. Sun, and K. Q. Weinberger, “On calibration of modern neural networks,” in Proc. 34th Int. Conf. Mach. Learn. (ICML), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, vol. 70, 2017, pp. 1321–1330. [Online]. Available: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v70/guo17a.html
entries.supported_claim: Modern neural-network classification scores can be miscalibrated, and temperature scaling improved calibration on the studied classification tasks.
entries.limitation: A calibrated classification confidence is not automatically a probability of satisfying a two-corner pixel tolerance or of a hidden corner being physically observable.

entries.limitation: The publication motivates the optimizer; the reported cassette training settings and outcomes are project measurements.

entries.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems
entries.supported_claim: Quality Focal Loss supports continuous quality targets and weights classification loss by the magnitude of score-target disagreement.
entries.limitation: The prepared cassette trial retains native pose-aware target construction and only changes the classification objective. It does not reproduce the complete GFL detector or distributed box representation; it also changes aggregate loss scale. Results remain pending.
